title: Safe or risky?
instruction: Sort what is safe with games and what is risky.

items.text: You download the game from the official store
items.why: The store checks apps. The risk is smaller, though not zero.

items.text: A cheat from a link in a comment under a video
items.why: An untrusted source, a classic Trojan horse.

items.text: A mod wants to run as the computer’s administrator
items.why: With administrator rights a program can do anything on the computer.

items.text: You install a game update as soon as it comes out
items.why: An update closes holes that attackers know about.

items.text: A torch game wants access to your contacts
items.why: It doesn’t need contacts to shine a light. So why would it want them?

items.text: Your saves are in the game’s cloud too
items.why: A copy somewhere else: it survives a lost or broken phone.

items.text: You turn off your antivirus because the cheat “doesn’t like it”
items.why: That is exactly what malware needs.

debrief: An antivirus alone doesn’t keep you safe. Your choices do: a trusted source, updates and permissions that make sense.
